full_judgment:
7. In the background of these facts and circumstances, Mr Rafique-ul-Huq, the learned Counsel on behalf of the respondent No. 3, firstly, submits that there is no question of opposing the prayer for condonation of delay for holding the AGMs for the years 1998 and 1999 but also prays that the delay in holding the Annual General Meeting for the year 2000 should also be condoned. He, however, refers to different part of the petition, specially paragraph 14, and submits that the petition itself brought serious allegations against the respondent No. 3 which, according to the learned Counsel, was absolutely false, that there are so many cases, down from the Court of Assistant Judge up to the Appellate Division which only highlight the atmosphere in the UCBL and its Board so much so that it is not at all congenial for holding the meeting as well as the election of the UCBL under the Chairmanship of Mr Zafar Ahmed Chowdhury, the present Chairman. He also submits that even the Bangladesh Bank earlier drew up a proceeding against the present Chairman under section 46 of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 on various allegations which was, however, declared illegal on a technical ground but not on the merits of the allegations. He submits that although the said proceeding was declared illegal not because the allegations raised by the central bank was wrong or without foundation but because of an earlier order passed by the Appellate Division to maintain the composition of the Board till disposal of the injunction matter, as such, he submits that when such serious allegations were raised against a person by the Bangladesh Bank he should not be allowed to chair the Annual General Meetings of a reputed bank like UCBL. Besides, he submits that the added respondent No. 3 who was the first Chairman of the Board of the UCBL also claims, in his suit, to be the present Chairman, He further submits that it would be better in the overall interest of the UCBL which is a well known bank in Bangladesh, to appoint a neutral person to preside over its Annual General Meetings, without prejudice to anybody as it was done in similar other occasions. In support of his contention the learned Counsel refers to the decisions reported in AIR 1952 Mad 60, PLD 1968 Dhaka 610, 38 DLR (AD) 296 and also 52 DLR 141. 

 Sankar Prasad Mitra, J in the matter of Ruttonjee & Co Ltd (1970) 40 Comp Cas491, while rejecting an application under section 186 of the Indian Companies Act, 1956 (equivalent to section 85(3) of the Companies Act, 1994) held at page 515: 

 In the case of Bengal and Assam Investors Ltd vs JK Eastern Industries Private Ltd AIR 1956 (Cal) 658, PB Mukharji, J also considered section 186 of the Indian Companies Act and held as follows: 

 Our Appellate Division considered the jurisdiction of the company Judge in directing to hold an Annual General Meeting under the Chairmanship of a neutral person in the case of Ghyasuddin Ahmed vs Faruque 38 DLR (AD) 296. In that case, the company Judge found that there was two groups of share-holders, that Board meeting was not held on the date notified and even when held on the next date, it was not attended by one group and that litigations ensued between the two groups. Fazle Munim, CJ considered the ambit of section 76(3) and section 73(3) of the Companies Act, 1913, at paragraph 17, in this manner: 

 "(16) Were I to accede to a request that this Court should call or hold and conduct Company meetings because one set of shareholders or directors are quarrelling with another set of shareholders or directors, then I shall be opening the easy door for every kind of officious intervention because then the easiest way for anyone, be he of the majority or of the minority in the Company, will be to make an allegation against any of the existing directors in an application under section 186, Companies Act asking this Court to call, hold and conduct such meetings. I do not think that was the intention of the Act, and I am also satisfied that is not the construction of the expressions appearing in section 186, Companies Act."
